Register: Always a Customer

The one field this endpoint deliberately never reads from the request body is the role it creates.

POST /auth/register is the first place this project creates a User row at all through the API — and a deliberate design decision shows up immediately: it can only ever create a customer.

// Figure 4.5: registering, and the service call it delegates to (src/controllers/auth.controller.js and src/services/user.service.js, excerpt)
export const register = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const user = await userService.createCustomer(req.body);
  const token = signToken({ sub: user.id, role: user.role });
  sendResource(res, { user, token }, 201);
});

export const createCustomer = async ({ name, email, password }) => {
  const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(password);
  return prisma.user.create({
    data: { name, email, password: hashedPassword, role: 'customer' },
    select: PUBLIC_FIELDS,
  });
};

registerSchema (validators/auth.validators.js) has no role field at all — even if a request body includes one, Zod's default behavior strips unknown keys rather than erroring on them, so req.body reaching createCustomer never has one to read. And createCustomer itself hard-codes role: 'customer' in the data it sends to Prisma, rather than trusting anything from its argument for that field. Both are deliberate, not redundant: a public, unauthenticated endpoint that let a request body choose its own role would let anyone register straight in as an admin. Real agents and admins get created some other way (Lesson 2's seed script, for now) — never through a route the whole internet can reach.

hashPassword (previous topic) runs before anything reaches Prisma, and PUBLIC_FIELDS (user.service.js) — { id, name, email, role, createdAt } — is what select limits the returned row to, so the hash itself never makes a round trip back into a response body. signToken({ sub: user.id, role: user.role }) immediately after is what lets a client start making authenticated requests right away, without needing a separate login call straight after registering.
